items.title: The superseded 1560->1960 two-span arc and its sim machinery are deleted outright
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-898 (2)): retire outright, no legacy field.

WHY. The arc is chosen at era_minus_one.cpp:25-36 and built at 298-315 (stop = epoch, boundary = epoch - industrial_years, span1_band_ceiling = medieval, two tick bands). Machinery only it uses: history_sim_params::boundary_year and span1_band_ceiling (history_sim.hpp:182-192); sim_band_ceiling (history_sim.hpp:4288-4289; history_sim.cpp:249-258) and the ceiling argument threaded through build_stack (history_sim.cpp:289-300, 4281, 4286, 5762, 5799); the furnace-before-boundary note (history_sim.cpp:6980-6995); the two-span half of BL-976's protection derivation (~7849-7916 — the broadcast half STAYS, seed_national_tariffs reads it at hard_coded_world.cpp:1808-1821); world_params::industrial_years (hard_coded_world.hpp:96-100).

THE WORK. Delete era_minus_one_has_industrial_span, the two-span branch, industrial_years, boundary_year, span1_band_ceiling, sim_band_ceiling and the ceiling parameter; keep the protection field and broadcast. Harnesses that build the arc are rewritten or retired by the harness item: world_determinism R4 (636-685, digest '1960/two-span' at :666), era_world_harness R5 (113-118, 250-272), history_sweep's two-span reporting (1037-1075, the BL-760 section from 2159, 2509-2520, 3317), ownership_class.cpp:534, demand_census.cpp:1436, haulage_measure.cpp:178.

DONE WHEN. grep industrial_years|boundary_year|span1_band_ceiling|has_industrial_span is empty in src/ and tools/; the '1960/two-span' digest is gone; the epoch-0 digests are unchanged.

items.title: One play-handoff struct carries every row of What crosses into play, each carried or stated deferred, and world setup reads only it
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 46 planned row 7).

WHY. industrialisation_output is an empty subclass of exploration_output (history_sim.hpp:5132-5134; its comment :5118-5122 says it 'does not yet carry' the play list). World setup reads four things from it: grudges, surviving corridors, treasuries, the live settlement (hard_coded_world.cpp:1493-1496). Row by row (INDUSTRIALISATION.md:700-720) today: nations/polity map READ (:1621, :1720); GDP not read (only treasury, nation_generation.cpp:1148-1171); regime stub not read (ideology from the furnace tercile, settlement.cpp:1654); garrisons partly (size from treasury, nation_generation.cpp:1415-1418); corporate web/charter budget not read (app.cpp:1063-1070 — BL-1042 changes this); price field/demand weights not read (base prices, :2287-2290); tariff posture called (:1820) but zero on the shipped arc (history_sim.cpp:7858); road tiers partly (ancient_tier rule road_generation.cpp:198, not the sim's c.tier history_sim.cpp:7782; no rail rung); culture shares partly (plurality for naming only :1655, :1665); standing war conditions not found; campaign tech state not read (polity::industry_mask history_sim.hpp:2728); per-nation Alarm not found; sea lanes not found; network strength not read; depleted reserves not read; grudges as sentiment READ (:1757-1806).

THE WORK. A play_handoff struct holding every row, each flagged carried or deferred with its reason; built from industrialisation_output plus setup; world setup takes only it, not the loose kepler_* locals; validated as BL-969 validates handoffs; the contract table written into INDUSTRIALISATION.md. Land it EARLY: every carry-row item then adds one field to it.

DONE WHEN. Every row is a field or on the stated-deferred list; a harness asserts the four current reads come through the struct (industrialisation_sim_harness.cpp:1193+); a grep finds no setup read of sim state outside it; digests unchanged.

items.title: National ideology, qualification, focus and the corporation focus pivot read Beat 1's industry points, not the calendar lag
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-898 (4)).

WHY (a structural zero on the shipped arc). Stage 4 skips when the settlement stop year is before 1700 (settlement.cpp:1232, :1325), so every region keeps industrial_lag_years = -1 (settlement.hpp:321); the furnace loop skips negative lags (history_sim.cpp:7012); nothing industrialises and median_industrial_year stays 0 (:7796-7805). So derive_national_character (settlement.cpp:1590-1683) sees no first furnace: every nation Isolationist (:1654), qualification 0.05 (:1675), the early-industrialiser focus bump (:1649-1651) never fires, focus falls back to all regions (:1635-1637). focus_from_region (settlement.cpp:2148; called corporation_generation.cpp:1693, :3106) needs median > 0 and never fires. Isolationist maps to ownership_class::closed (corporation_generation.cpp:1494). The road lattice's tier gate reads the qualification percentile (road_generation.cpp:298, :414).

THE WORK. A points-based industrialisation reading per region (region::industry_points, settlement.hpp:455, accrued history_sim.cpp:3496-3508, treasury share :1056-1092) — a threshold or a within-world rank, DESIGN AT THE CUT; carried on the handoff; first furnace, terciles, qualification, focus and focus_from_region re-derived from it; Stage 4's calendar lag retired with the two-span arc.

DONE WHEN. Over the 16 library seeds: ideology takes more than one value, qualification is not 0.05 everywhere, the pivot fires for some corporations; the ownership-class spread is reported; lands behind the sprint's switch.

items.title: Each Empires force that is off after 1200 is measured on the Exploration and Industrialisation spans, then ruled on
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-898 (9)): measure, then decide.

WHY. Exploration's params are the struct defaults plus a few overrides (era_minus_one.cpp:372-413) and Industrialisation copies them (:432), so every Empires override (:65-296) is off after 1200 except settle_requires_razed_ground and city_states_by_population_threshold (:409-410). Off (history_sim.hpp defaults): amphibious_weight_crossing and sea_legs_* (:1171, :1196); trade_income_per_class (:1266); army_upkeep_per_1000_heads, unpaid_army_disband_q, road_build_material_cost (:1309, :1316, :1333); supply_upgrade_* (:1788-1797); secession_supply_floor_q (:1361); universal_creed_* (:1398-1433), schism_min_regions (:1464); centre_chain_reach and its rebates (:1002); w_aggr_q (:1488), w_fear_q (:1528), turbulence_lean (:1630). Possible post-1200 analogues (inferred from names, confirm): exploration_upkeep_enabled with standing_army_upkeep_per_1000_heads_year_q (army upkeep); post_road_treasury_cost (road build cost); deterrence_alarm_weight_q (fear). industrialisation_sim_harness.cpp:1147-1188 asserts all stay off in the span.

THE WORK. Add each to exploration_sweep's --set whitelist (apply_sets, :770-781); sweep off vs the Empires value through 1960 on the 16 library seeds; read battles, secessions, schisms, treasuries, industry points per span; set the EMPIRES_ONLY guard aside for the sweep only. Then an NR entry per force for Ben.

DONE WHEN. A table per setting (span x off/on x metric deltas, 16 seeds) is filed with Ben's rulings; industrialisation_sim_params and the harness list match the rulings.

items.title: Markets open on the generated price field, and household demand is weighted by the catchment's culture
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-898 (7), carry row 1).

WHY. Generation produces region::scarcity_q and culture_preference (culture_good_preference, history_sim.hpp:4610, one row per culture and good), crossing at history_sim.hpp:4965, :5036. The campaign reads neither (nothing in hard_coded_world, market_clearing or corporation_generation). Markets open at mc.price = mc.base_price (hard_coded_world.cpp:2289, :2297) plus only the endemic gradient (:2302-2358). inject_population_demand (market_clearing.cpp:237-292) applies one registry basket to every centre (:257) — no per-market weight. Preference is keyed on region_class (farm/ore/energy/port, settlement.hpp:65-71), not resource_type.

THE WORK. A region_class -> resource mapping table (design-owed, MARKETS.md property 5 — settle at the cut); a per-market weight array from the population-weighted culture shares of each market's catchment (region shares only; centres carry none until Beat 2); stored and serialised on market_component; basket[r] multiplied by it at market_clearing.cpp:282; opening mc.price seeded from scarcity_q and the weights. Behind the sprint switch.

DONE WHEN. On a 1960 world the cross-market spread of mc.price[r] is non-zero for a named good; two markets of different culture plurality inject different demand for one good at one scale; money conservation holds.

items.title: The Industrialisation span derives each nation's tariff posture, and a tariff is charged where goods actually cross a border
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-898 (7), carry row 2).

WHY (three gaps). DERIVATION: protection_q is written only when boundary_year != INT64_MIN (history_sim.cpp:7858, :7876); industrialisation_sim_params builds on exploration_sim_params (era_minus_one.cpp:432), which leaves it INT64_MIN (comment :321-322), so the 1960 close writes 0 and seed_national_tariffs (law.cpp:158, called hard_coded_world.cpp:1820) skips every nation (law.cpp:174). The Industry tree's tariff_pressure is pinned 0 (history_sim.cpp:8809). INDUSTRIALISATION.md:137-143 says the derivation from scarcity_q, trade_flows and culture_preference is owed to this phase. CHARGING: the only charge is on matched trades with a buyer domiciled abroad (market_clearing.cpp:1257-1291), dormant in play. CONVOY DUTY: MARKETS.md:784-794 rules a duty on convoy arrival and retires the matched-trade charge; not built (credit_arrived_convoys, supply_system.cpp:151); BL-1005 was cancelled.

THE WORK. A span-side derivation of protection_q from the three inputs at the end-of-run block (history_sim.cpp:7857ff) or the handoff; the broadcast (:7913-7919) then feeds derive_national_protection (settlement.cpp:1405) unchanged. SCOPE CALL AT THE CUT: the convoy-arrival duty (quantity x destination last price x nation_tariff_rate, a treasury transfer) and retiring the matched-trade block are what make a posture bite in play — carry them here, or state play-side charging deferred.

DONE WHEN. On a 1960 world at least one LAW-IMPORT-TARIFF-* law exists; if the duty is in scope, a cross-border convoy raises the destination treasury by exactly the owner's debit (money_conservation extended) and the matched-trade block is gone.

items.title: A culture lens shows each province's people, checkered where two are nearly even, and survives a save

items.title: The nation summary shows treasury, GDP and the nation's grudges
items.design:

items.title: The landscape search's seed candidate is placed by network strength, BL-879's unmet clause
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-898 (7), carry row 5); BL-879 closed complete with this clause unbuilt.

WHY. The seed candidate is arbitrary: sp.start.placement_seed = sp.seed (app.cpp:1061); landscape_candidate has only count, seed and tier (landscape_search.hpp:88-99); placement uses that RNG seed (landscape_search.cpp:211, :213). Of the three signals the row names, only corridor degree is computed, and only to gate markets (hard_coded_world.cpp:2153-2166, kMarketJunctionDegree = 3); corridor uses are carried (era_timelapse.hpp:473); sea-lane traffic does not exist (sea-lanes item). app.cpp:1063-1070's 'industry points do not exist yet' is stale (BL-1041) — BL-1042 rewrites it.

THE WORK. Per-region network strength (corridor uses, lane traffic once it exists, junction degree) computed at setup as a generation-time index beside gen_settlement; a 'seed from network' mode in landscape_search_params biasing the seed candidate's specialist and firm homes toward strong regions, deterministically, perturbation axes unchanged; the census BL-879's done-when asks for; the harness_params.hpp shipped_search_params mirror updated with the app.

DONE WHEN. Seed-candidate sites correlate positively with junction degree over the 16 seeds; the winner is identical across thread counts (landscape_search_harness R2).

items.title: The sim records its sea legs, and the campaign opens with lanes on the water they crossed
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-898 (7), carry row 6). Design: EXPLORATION.md:330-358. The largest carry row: the sim records nothing yet. BL-876 was cancelled.

WHY. No sea-leg record in the sim (grep sea_lane in src is empty; only the sea_legs_* ration params, history_sim.hpp:1173-1223); history_corridor has no water flag (era_timelapse.hpp:469-484). Traversal uses a flat sea_leg_cost = 2.5f (logistics.cpp:18); tile_traversal_cost (logistics.cpp:94-100) already multiplies the water base by road_traversal_multiplier(tc.road_level), so a tier on water tiles discounts with no pathfinding change.

THE WORK. Record sea legs in the sim (amphibious supply, purchase-party crossings, metropole-holding traffic) as a counted table; fold it into the play handoff with validator rules; at setup stamp water tiles along each leg with a lane tier once traffic passes a threshold, by analogy with stamp_history_roads (road_generation.hpp:103); serialise it as its own field rather than overloading road_level.

DONE WHEN. Lane tiles on a 1960 world > 0 and counted in the report; A* cost between two lane-joined ports falls below the unlaned cost; reach crosses the lane; digests move only behind the switch.

items.title: Reserves open depleted where history worked the ground
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-898 (7), carry row 7). Design: INDUSTRIALISATION.md:724-729, EXPLORATION.md:653-670 — the formula itself is unwritten; BL-945 was cancelled.

WHY. resource_remaining is seeded at tile generation as deposit x deposit_reserve_factor = 400 (tile_generation.cpp:18-22, :2596-2605), before history runs, so the reserve ignores it. The inputs already cross on region: founded_year and industrial_year (settlement.hpp:302-304), dominant (:266), and corridor uses. resource_remaining is folded into state_hash (world.cpp:137).

THE WORK. Write the formula into INDUSTRIALISATION.md FIRST (named inputs, named arithmetic — a design step at the cut, Ben's call); then a pure retrofit_depletion(world, settlement, params) at setup after nations, scaling each tile's reserve by years held, class and industrialisation (Beat 1 points, per the industrialisation item); a harness assertion.

DONE WHEN. Mean resource_remaining / (deposit x 400) < 1 on long-worked industrialised regions and == 1 on never-settled ground; the doc formula matches the code constants.

items.title: Each corporation opens holding the campaign techs its nation's Industry mask earned
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-898 (7), carry row 8): per CORPORATION through the existing earned_techs gates, not per nation. NOVELTY/SCOPE FLAG owed at the cut (NEXT_SESSION): there is no per-nation consumer and no IN-* -> E*-* mapping; the mapping needs a design session with Ben.

WHY. polity::industry_mask is 45 nodes (history_sim.hpp:2719-2728; node_count industry_tree_data.hpp:12), crossing in industrialisation_output::polities, read by no setup code. world::earned_techs is per-corporation and empty at setup (world.hpp:458-464), written only by advance_tech_gates (tech_gate.cpp:175-205), which also appends each tech's modify_scalar effects to corp_modifiers. The campaign gate table has 4 gates: E0-ML-01, E0-EC-01, E1-EC-01, E0-EC-03 (tech_gate.cpp:33, :79, :113, :137). The Lua campaign tree (tech_tree.hpp, load_from_lua) feeds the F9 viewer. Industry nodes unlock works rows and roster bands (industry_tree_data.hpp:57-93); IN-SP-3m 'The Renewed Line' opens the campaign tree (:43). earned_techs is erased when a corporation is regenerated (corporation_generation.cpp:2084), and the landscape search regenerates rosters (landscape_search.cpp:211).

THE WORK. Design session: the IN-node -> campaign-tech mapping. Polity -> nation by the representative-polity tally used for grudges (hard_coded_world.cpp:1761-1790). Seed each corporation from its home_nation's mask AFTER the search winner is applied (after app.cpp:1076), not in world-gen, or the regeneration wipes it; seed through a helper that also appends the tech's modifiers; 'The Renewed Line held' opens the root. Check whether state_hash folds earned_techs (unverified).

DONE WHEN. On a 1960 world, corporations of a nation holding the mapped IN node have the mapped tech (has_tech) and its modifiers, corporations of one without it do not, and both survive save and load.

NR-885 (2026-09-17): the player is a corporation holding a seat. Not surveyed on 2026-09-19 on purpose: the design session sets its question, surface and data before any code read.

items.title: Density follows cities: the charter web at the ruled prices is too sparse to track cities across the markets — a design pass on the density knobs
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-22, NR-913, the pooling form): BL-1044 ships the unpooled web and its done-when is restated; 'density follows cities' becomes this item, a design pass of its own.

WHY. Beat 1's claim (INDUSTRIALISATION.md § 1) is that the charter budget is the stockpile, not headcount, so a web that follows cities proves something. Measured at the pins (650:2, 16 library seeds, industrialisation_sim_harness --through 1960 reading 1): rho(firms per market, catchment urban population) median 0.139 against rho(firms, good count) 0.167; urban beats goods on 5 of 16 worlds; the legacy web read 0.431 against 0.460 (BL-1029). The web holds a median 65 firms over 148 to 538 markets, so most markets hold none. A firm costs 1/650 of the whole stock and the stock is split over 5,000 to 15,000 carved centres, so most centres hold less than one firm's price and ~85% of every stock goes unspent. Pooling the stranded remainder (NR-913's measurement, charter_spend_params::pool, kept as an off-by-default switch) lifts the reading only to 0.186-0.211, because the density ceiling (120 a body, NR-902) then binds, and it moves the seat menu (pooled firms take ground before poorer centres' specialists).

THE QUESTION. Which knob makes density follow cities without breaking NR-908's live-play band: the density ceiling, the firm price (a centre-relative price rather than a share of the whole stock), where firms may anchor (a centre's market catchment rather than its own window), or the reading itself (per centre or per region rather than per market). Each has a tick cost, measured against BL-1044's 650:2 row.

DONE WHEN. A ruled knob and a reading: rho(firms, urban) above rho(firms, goods) on the median library world, the tick inside NR-908's band, the seat menu held at the anchor.
